resolution.title: Fix: Error when creating an attribute for a group in “All shops” context with multiple shops
resolution.description: This PR fixes an issue in AttributeGroupChoiceProvider where the service could receive a `null` shop ID in valid contexts (e.g. _All shops_ or back office initialization). ticket.bug:

ticket.title: CsvFileReader service fails with "You have requested a non-existent service 'session'"
ticket.bug: When trying to use the service `prestashop.core.import.csv_file_reader`, which points to the class `PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Import\File\CsvFileReader`, the following error occurs: `You have requested a non-existent service "session"` A screenshot of the error is attached.

resolution.title: Fix: CsvFileReader service fails with "You have requested a non-existent service 'session'"
resolution.description: This PR fixes an issue in the `prestashop.core.import.csv_file_reader` service definition where the `session` service was accessed directly, causing a `"You have requested a non-existent service 'session'"` error in certain contexts.  The service definition has been updated to retrieve the session via `RequestStack`. This issue did not occur in PrestaShop 8 because the `session` service was still available.   Starting from **Symfony 5.3**, the direct `session` service has been deprecated and later removed in favor of accessing the session through `RequestStack`.  See: https://symfony.com/blog/new-in-symfony-5-3-session-service-deprecation
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the module [issue_csvfilereader.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24719955/issue_csvfilereader.zip)  2. Go to the module configuration page 3. You should no longer see the error.

ticket.title: Module update problem
ticket.bug: If you create an update for a module and in the update there is a need to hook/unhook the module from a hook, it doesn't work because the instance of the object (module) passed to the update function does not have the "id" attribute set.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the [issue40429.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24384071/issue40429.zip) module, which will be attached to the hookDisplayBackOfficeTop hook.
2. Go to the configuration and you will see: `This module is registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`.
3. Open the issue40429.php file and change
`$this->version = '1.0.0'` to `$this->version = '1.0.1'`.
4. Now go to _Module > Module Manager > Updates_.
5. Update the module. During the update, the system will "attempt" to detach the module from the `hookDisplayBackOfficeTop `hook.
6. Now go back to the module configuration, and you will still see: `This module is registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop` — instead, you should see: `This module is NOT registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`.

resolution.title: Fix: Module update problem
resolution.description: Since PrestaShop 9.0.2, the Modules page has been migrated to Symfony (see https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/36845), so module updates are now executed under a Symfony controller.  As the controller is no longer a legacy Controller, the Module constructor always resets the modules cache via `static::$modules_cache = null;`, because the following condition is always satisfied:  ```php if (!$this->context->controller instanceof Controller) {```  This PR prevents the modules cache from being reset in this context, ensuring module updates work correctly.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the [issue40429.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24384071/issue40429.zip) module, which will be attached to the hookDisplayBackOfficeTop hook. 2. Go to the configuration and you will see: `This module is registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`. 3. Open the issue40429.php file and change `$this->version = '1.0.0'` to `$this->version = '1.0.1'`. 4. Now go to _Module > Module Manager > Updates_. 5. Update the module. During the update, the system will "attempt" to detach the module from the `hookDisplayBackOfficeTop `hook. 6. Now go back to the module configuration, you should see: `This module is NOT registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Issue retrieving product price when adding the first specific_price
ticket.bug:
When a new **specific_price** is added and no other specific prices exist in the catalog, the product price retrieved inside the `hookActionObjectSpecificPriceAddAfter` hook does not take the newly added discount into account.

This happens because the configuration `PS_SPECIFIC_PRICE_FEATURE_ACTIVE` is set to 1 only after the specific_price is created. However, the `hookActionObjectSpecificPriceAddAfterhook` is executed before this configuration is updated.
As a result, when the hook attempts to retrieve the product price, the feature is still disabled (`NULL`) and the discount is not applied.
ticket.expected: The price retrieved inside the hook should correctly reflect the newly added specific_price, even when it is the first specific_price in the catalog.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the module [issue40255.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23959265/issue40255.zip).
2. Ensure that no specific prices exist in the catalog.
3. Open a product in edit mode.
4. In the Pricing section, add a new specific price.
5. When the popup reloads, you will see the message (added by the module): `Product price: FULL_PRICE Reduction: 0`
Instead, the price should reflect the applied discount, and **Reduction** should be different from 0.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/729963bf-689f-4cd9-86ae-633bb3549355

resolution.title: Fix: Issue retrieving product price when adding the first specific_price
resolution.description: This PR ensures that `PS_SPECIFIC_PRICE_FEATURE_ACTIVE` is enabled before inserting the first specific price, allowing hooks to correctly retrieve discounted prices. If the insertion fails, the previous configuration value is restored to avoid leaving the system in an inconsistent state.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the module [issue40255.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23959265/issue40255.zip).  2. Ensure that no specific prices exist in the catalog.  3. Open a product in edit mode.  4. In the Pricing section, add a new specific price.  5. When the popup reloads, you will see the message (added by the module): `Product price: DISCOUNTED_PRICE Reduction: REDUCTION`   You need to display the discounted price and the discount amount
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Order::getIdByCartId in OrderConfirmationControllerCore fails to query order_id when cached
ticket.bug:
When a payment module redirects to order-confirmation, the `OrderId` is fetched using:
`$this->id_order = Order::getIdByCartId((int) $this->id_cart);` https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1d97fcde1bf31d522cfbcfde904316da1d9088d6/controllers/front/OrderConfirmationController.php#L83

`Order::getIdByCartId` uses `$result = Db::getInstance()->getValue($sql);`, with the default of getValue being to use cache.
Now, in some clustered environments it's possible that the order is created by one node and the confirmation page is server by another; this seems to cause the `Order::getIdByCartId` to return a cached `false`, causing the confirmation page to do an early redirect, exiting early. https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1d97fcde1bf31d522cfbcfde904316da1d9088d6/controllers/front/OrderConfirmationController.php#L95

In my experiments, forcing `Order::getIdByCartId` to query a non cached result solves the issue.
ticket.steps:
1. Pay an order with a PSP that confirms the payment via S2S callbacks.
2. If the conditions align you will sometimes get redirected away from the confirmation page

resolution.title: Always request a non cached result in Order::getIdByCartId
resolution.description: This resolves an issue with the order-confirmation controller evident in clustered environments using cache. (see #40007)
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Deploy in a clustered environment with APCu cache enabled. 2. Enable a payment module which receives the payment validation via server-to-server communication from the PSP 3. Place an order, pay and get redirected to confirmation page (before the fix you sometimes will get redirected away from the order confirmation page |
resolution.author: ilsalvopss

ticket.title: Multishop: Deleting and recreating a combination removes the shared reference (new Product Page V2)
ticket.bug:
In a multishop setup with two shops (e.g., **B2C** and **B2B**), using the new product page (Product Page v2), if a product has an active combination for both shops, the following behavior occurs:

The product has an active combination with:
**Size**: S
**Reference**: REFERENCE

If I delete this combination from the **B2B** shop and then recreate it, the system reassigns the same combination (keeping the same ID). This behavior is correct and useful.

Issue: During this process, the system removes the value of the **Reference** (reference) field of the combination. Since the **Reference** field is unique across all shops, it should remain unchanged even after deleting and recreating the combination.

In my opinion, the system should preserve the reference value to avoid data loss and ensure proper management of combinations in a multishop context.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa953118-81a5-4c49-b6b3-38bbe4b77241
ticket.expected: The system should retain the value of the **Reference** (REFERENCE) field.
ticket.steps:
1. Set up a multishop configuration with at least two shops (e.g., B2C and B2B).
2. Create a product with an active combination shared across both shops:
**Size**: S
**Reference**: REFERENCE
3. Delete the combination from the B2B shop.
4. Recreate the same combination in the B2B shop.

resolution.title: Fix: Multishop: Deleting and recreating a combination removes the shared reference (new Product Page V2)
resolution.description: see: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/37840 - Note: The issue also occurs on the 9.0.x branch, so I performed the rebase by moving the PR to 9.0.x because PRs are no longer being merged on version 8.2.x.

ticket.title: Module update problem
ticket.bug: If you create an update for a module and in the update there is a need to hook/unhook the module from a hook, it doesn't work because the instance of the object (module) passed to the update function does not have the "id" attribute set.
ticket.steps:

4. Now go to _Module > Module Manager > Updates_.
5. Update the module. During the update, the system will "attempt" to detach the module from the `hookDisplayBackOfficeTop `hook.

resolution.description: Since PrestaShop 9.0.2, the Modules page has been migrated to Symfony (see https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/36845), so module updates are now executed under a Symfony controller.  As the controller is no longer a legacy Controller, the Module constructor always resets the modules cache via `static::$modules_cache = null;`, because the following condition is always satisfied:  ```php if (!$this->context->controller instanceof Controller) {```  This PR prevents the modules cache from being reset in this context, ensuring module updates work correctly.

During the update, the system will "attempt" to detach the module from the `hookDisplayBackOfficeTop `hook. 6. Now go back to the module configuration, you should see: `This module is NOT registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`.

ticket.title: Issue retrieving product price when adding the first specific_price
ticket.bug:
When a new **specific_price** is added and no other specific prices exist in the catalog, the product price retrieved inside the `hookActionObjectSpecificPriceAddAfter` hook does not take the newly added discount into account.

This happens because the configuration `PS_SPECIFIC_PRICE_FEATURE_ACTIVE` is set to 1 only after the specific_price is created. However, the `hookActionObjectSpecificPriceAddAfterhook` is executed before this configuration is updated.
As a result, when the hook attempts to retrieve the product price, the feature is still disabled (`NULL`) and the discount is not applied.
ticket.expected: The price retrieved inside the hook should correctly reflect the newly added specific_price, even when it is the first specific_price in the catalog.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the module [issue40255.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23959265/issue40255.zip).
2. Ensure that no specific prices exist in the catalog.
3. Open a product in edit mode.
4. In the Pricing section, add a new specific price.
5. When the popup reloads, you will see the message (added by the module): `Product price: FULL_PRICE Reduction: 0`
Instead, the price should reflect the applied discount, and **Reduction** should be different from 0.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/729963bf-689f-4cd9-86ae-633bb3549355

resolution.title: Fix: Issue retrieving product price when adding the first specific_price
resolution.description: This PR ensures that `PS_SPECIFIC_PRICE_FEATURE_ACTIVE` is enabled before inserting the first specific price, allowing hooks to correctly retrieve discounted prices. If the insertion fails, the previous configuration value is restored to avoid leaving the system in an inconsistent state.

ticket.title: Order::getIdByCartId in OrderConfirmationControllerCore fails to query order_id when cached
ticket.bug:
When a payment module redirects to order-confirmation, the `OrderId` is fetched using:
`$this->id_order = Order::getIdByCartId((int) $this->id_cart);` https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1d97fcde1bf31d522cfbcfde904316da1d9088d6/controllers/front/OrderConfirmationController.php#L83

`Order::getIdByCartId` uses `$result = Db::getInstance()->getValue($sql);`, with the default of getValue being to use cache.
Now, in some clustered environments it's possible that the order is created by one node and the confirmation page is server by another; this seems to cause the `Order::getIdByCartId` to return a cached `false`, causing the confirmation page to do an early redirect, exiting early. https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1d97fcde1bf31d522cfbcfde904316da1d9088d6/controllers/front/OrderConfirmationController.php#L95

In my experiments, forcing `Order::getIdByCartId` to query a non cached result solves the issue.
ticket.steps:
1. Pay an order with a PSP that confirms the payment via S2S callbacks.
2. If the conditions align you will sometimes get redirected away from the confirmation page

resolution.title: Always request a non cached result in Order::getIdByCartId
resolution.description: This resolves an issue with the order-confirmation controller evident in clustered environments using cache. (see #40007)
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Deploy in a clustered environment with APCu cache enabled. 2. Enable a payment module which receives the payment validation via server-to-server communication from the PSP 3. Place an order, pay and get redirected to confirmation page (before the fix you sometimes will get redirected away from the order confirmation page |
resolution.author: ilsalvopss

ticket.title: Performance Issue: Heavy SQL Query in OrderCountriesChoiceProvider Slows Down Orders Grid
ticket.bug:
Describe the Bug:
Instead, on every page load the following query runs—twice—processing ~110,698 rows and taking ~759,248 ms:

sql

SELECT SQL_NO_CACHE DISTINCT c.id_country, cl.`name`
FROM `ps_orders` o
INNER JOIN `ps_address` a
    ON a.id_address = o.id_address_delivery
INNER JOIN `ps_country` c
    ON a.id_country = c.id_country
INNER JOIN `ps_country_lang` cl
    ON (c.`id_country` = cl.`id_country`
        AND cl.`id_lang` = 3)
ORDER BY cl.name ASC

src/Adapter/Form/ChoiceProvider/OrderCountriesChoiceProvider.php.

ticket.title: Multishop: Deleting and recreating a combination removes the shared reference (new Product Page V2)
ticket.bug:
In a multishop setup with two shops (e.g., **B2C** and **B2B**), using the new product page (Product Page v2), if a product has an active combination for both shops, the following behavior occurs:

The product has an active combination with:
**Size**: S
**Reference**: REFERENCE

If I delete this combination from the **B2B** shop and then recreate it, the system reassigns the same combination (keeping the same ID). This behavior is correct and useful.

Issue: During this process, the system removes the value of the **Reference** (reference) field of the combination. Since the **Reference** field is unique across all shops, it should remain unchanged even after deleting and recreating the combination.

In my opinion, the system should preserve the reference value to avoid data loss and ensure proper management of combinations in a multishop context.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa953118-81a5-4c49-b6b3-38bbe4b77241
ticket.expected: The system should retain the value of the **Reference** (REFERENCE) field.
ticket.steps:
1. Set up a multishop configuration with at least two shops (e.g., B2C and B2B).
2. Create a product with an active combination shared across both shops:
**Size**: S
**Reference**: REFERENCE
3. Delete the combination from the B2B shop.
4. Recreate the same combination in the B2B shop.

resolution.title: Fix: Multishop: Deleting and recreating a combination removes the shared reference (new Product Page V2)
resolution.description: see: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/37840 - Note: The issue also occurs on the 9.0.x branch, so I performed the rebase by moving the PR to 9.0.x because PRs are no longer being merged on version 8.2.x.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Set up a multishop configuration with at least two shops (e.g., B2C and B2B). 2. ticket.steps:
1. Create a module that hooks into `actionEmailSendBefore`.
2. Attempt to access the `replyToName` parameter within the hook.
3. Observe that the `replyToName` parameter is not available, while other parameters like `replyTo` are present.
ticket.versions: This issue affects all versions of PrestaShop up to and including the latest development versions (1.7, 8.2).

resolution.title: Add replyToName parameter to Hook actionEmailSendBefore
resolution.description: This PR adds the missing `replyToName` parameter to the `actionEmailSendBefore` hook. This parameter is already present in the `Mail::send()` method but was not being passed to the hook, limiting the ability of modules to modify the reply-to name of outgoing emails.
resolution.author: tups

ticket.title: Product customization text appears as raw HTML in order confirmation email (order_conf)
ticket.bug:
When a customer places an order for a customized product in Prestashop, the order confirmation email (order_conf) displays the product customization text as raw HTML rather than showing the text formatted correctly. 

Checkout video
[checkout.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f99d86f-3360-4ef9-b8ec-b88e486eafdd)

Screenshot email
![Email](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f573d4a0-a766-4606-b499-28e40f06d845)
ticket.steps:
1. Log in to a Prestashop installation (version XYZ).
2. Add a product with a customization option (e.g., custom text).
3. Place an order for the customized product.
4. Receive the order confirmation email (order_conf).
5. Notice that the product customization text in the email is displayed as raw HTML.
